variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
max_users = 100
current_user = 'Alice'

# Variables are dynamically typed
current_user = 'Bob'

# Constants start with a capital letter
MAX_FILE_SIZE = 1024

# Global (avoid), Instance, Class variables
$global_var = 1
@instance_var = 2
@@class_var = 3
variables.notes: Use snake_case for local variables. Reassigning constants generates a warning.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
str = 'Hello'
num = 42
float = 3.14
bool = true
nil_val = nil
sym = :my_symbol
array = [1, 2, 3]
hash = { key: 'value' }
data_types.notes: Everything in Ruby is an object. Symbols are immutable, reusable constants represented by a name.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
a = 10 + 5
b = 10 ** 2

# Equality
is_equal = (a == 15)

# Safe navigation operator
len = some_obj&.property&.length

# Conditional assignment
value ||= 'default'
operators.notes: Use '&.' to avoid NoMethodError on nil objects. '||=' sets a variable only if it is nil or false.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
score = 85

if score >= 90
  puts 'A'
elsif score >= 80
  puts 'B'
else
  puts 'C'
end

# Unless statement
puts 'Fail' unless score >= 50

# Pattern matching (Ruby 2.7+)
case score
in 90..100 then puts 'A'
in 80...90 then puts 'B'
end
conditionals.notes: Ruby supports statement modifiers (e.g., puts 'hi' if true). Pattern matching provides powerful object deconstruction.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
items = ['a', 'b', 'c']

# Each block (preferred)
items.each do |item|
  puts item
end

# For loop (rarely used)
for item in items
  puts item
end
for_loop.notes: Idiomatic Ruby uses 'each' with blocks instead of traditional 'for' loops.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
count = 0

while count < 5
  puts count
  count += 1
end

# Until loop
until count == 0
  count -= 1
end
while_loop.notes: Ruby also supports 'until', which loops as long as the condition is false.

functions.title: Functions
functions.notes: Methods return the value of the last evaluated expression implicitly. Use keyword arguments for clarity.

arrays.title: Arrays
arrays.code:
numbers = [1, 2, 3]
numbers << 4 # Append

# Array methods
doubled = numbers.map { |n| n * 2 }
evens = numbers.select(&:even?)

# Syntax sugar for array of strings
words = %w[apple banana cherry]
arrays.notes: Arrays are highly versatile. Use enumerable methods like map, select, reduce.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
# Hashes act as maps
user_roles = {
  alice: 'admin',
  bob: 'user'
}

user_roles[:charlie] = 'guest'

# Fetch with default value
role = user_roles.fetch(:dave, 'unknown')
maps.notes: Symbols are typically used as Hash keys. 'fetch' is preferred over '[]' to handle missing keys predictably.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
begin
  raise StandardError, 'Something went wrong'
rescue StandardError => e
  puts e.message
ensure
  # Cleanup logic
end

# Inline rescue
val = might_fail rescue 'default_value'
error_handling.notes: Catch 'StandardError', not 'Exception', to avoid trapping system-level errors.
